metadataConvention: Solo artists: birth/death years and birthplace. Bands: formation year and origin city.

entries.claim: Taylor Swift recorded a cover of Earth, Wind & Fire’s “September”.

sources.title: NPR / WBGO: Taylor Swift Covers Earth, Wind & Fire’s September
sources.evidence: Stephen Thompson reports the Spotify Singles cover in his April 2018 review.

sources.title: Library of Congress: Rickey Vincent on September
sources.evidence: The recording-history essay identifies Swift among artists who covered the Earth, Wind & Fire song. It documents the original’s R&B success.

entries.claim: Madonna and Stephen Bray drew on Sly and the Family Stone’s funk for “Express Yourself”.

sources.title: Rhino: May 1989 — Madonna Releases Express Yourself
sources.evidence: The record-label history names the co-writers and describes the song as their tribute to Sly and the Family Stone.

sources.title: Attitude: Ten reasons Like a Prayer remains an all-time classic
sources.evidence: The album retrospective explicitly identifies Sly and the Family Stone’s funk as inspiration for the Stephen Bray co-write.

entries.claim: Eminem’s “My Name Is” uses the riff from Labi Siffre’s funk recording “I Got The…”.

sources.title: MusicRadar: Chas and Dave played on a classic Eminem track
sources.evidence: The article identifies the Siffre recording, its session players, and its use by Dr. Dre for My Name Is; it calls the source track funk.

sources.title: Buffalo Toronto Public Media: Labi Siffre & Eminem
sources.evidence: The programme description explicitly names I Got The… as the source used in My Name Is.

entries.claim: Amy Winehouse recorded the jazz standard “Moody’s Mood for Love” on her debut album Frank.

sources.title: NME: The Amy Winehouse Band on why she was so special
sources.evidence: Bassist Dale Davis discusses Winehouse’s cover on Frank and rehearsing it with her. Opened through Python urllib because web open returned 403.

sources.title: Beat: Frank is a testament to the brilliance of Amy Winehouse
sources.evidence: The independent album retrospective identifies Moody’s Mood for Love among the jazz-standard covers on her debut.

entries.claim: Adele recorded Bob Dylan’s “Make You Feel My Love”.

sources.title: Rolling Stone: Every Adele Song, Ranked — Make You Feel My Love
sources.evidence: The Make You Feel My Love entry identifies Dylan as the writer of the cover on Adele’s debut; opened the article again at line 500 to reach the entry.

sources.title: SRF: Adele bringt Emotionen in Dylans Song
sources.evidence: The broadcaster compares Adele’s recording with Dylan’s original and explicitly credits his songwriting.

entries.claim: Ed Sheeran learned Eminem’s The Marshall Mathers LP by heart as a child, practising its rapid rap delivery.

sources.title: ABC News: How Eminem Helped Ed Sheeran Overcome Stuttering
sources.evidence: Reports Sheeran’s 2015 speech: he memorised the album before age ten and copied its rapid, melodic, percussive delivery.

sources.title: The Standard: Ed Sheeran on Eminem and his childhood stutter
sources.evidence: Reports a separate 2023 Howard Stern interview in which Sheeran recalls learning and repeatedly rapping the same album.

entries.claim: Billie Eilish names the Beatles as a formative musical influence, having grown up listening to them.

sources.title: NME: Billie Eilish — Glastonbury cover interview
sources.evidence: In the 2022 interview Eilish credits the Beatles with raising her musically and inspiring her love of music. Opened via Python urllib after web returned 403.

sources.title: MusicRadar: Billie Eilish names the Beatles song she wishes she had written
sources.evidence: Reports a separate 2024 BBC interview where Eilish names the Beatles her greatest inspiration and childhood listening.

sources.title: Johnny Cash: Rock Island Line — official recording catalogue
sources.evidence: The official catalogue documents Cash’s released recording. Its introductory tollgate narrative is the feature discussed in the Library of Congress analysis.

sources.title: Library of Congress: From Mule-een to New Orleans — What Was Lead Belly Saying?
sources.evidence: Stephen Winick traces the song to Kelly Pace’s Arkansas prison work group and specifically identifies Cash’s version as learned from Donegan rather than directly from Lead Belly.

entries.claim: Dolly Parton recorded the Beatles’ “Let It Be” with Paul McCartney and Ringo Starr for Rockstar.

sources.title: Dolly Parton: Let It Be release announcement
sources.evidence: The official announcement identifies the Beatles cover and McCartney and Starr’s participation on the Rockstar recording.

sources.title: Reuters / The Fiji Times: Surviving Beatles join Dolly Parton on Let It Be
sources.evidence: Reuters reports the released cover, the album, and the two Beatles’ musical contributions; this is independent newsroom coverage of the recording.

entries.claim: For “Dancing Queen”, ABBA took rhythmic inspiration from soul singer George McCrae’s “Rock Your Baby”.

sources.title: Library of Congress: Carl Magnus Palm on Arrival
sources.evidence: The historian explains that ABBA listened to McCrae’s hit to make the Dancing Queen groove more danceable.

sources.title: Rolling Stone: ABBA — Dancing Queen
sources.evidence: The song entry explicitly credits the hit by soul singer McCrae as inspiration for Dancing Queen.

entries.claim: BTS leader RM counts Eminem among the rappers who influenced him.

sources.title: El País: Interview with BTS leader RM
sources.evidence: The 2023 interview explicitly identifies Eminem among RM’s cited influences, in the discussion of his aspiration to become a rapper.

sources.title: Rolling Stone Korea: RM and Pharrell Williams in conversation
sources.evidence: Brian Hiatt’s introduction, available in English below the Korean text, identifies Eminem among the musicians who drew the young RM into music.

entries.claim: George Michael recorded “I Knew You Were Waiting (For Me)” as a duet with Aretha Franklin.

sources.title: Recording Academy: George Michael
sources.evidence: The artist profile names the Franklin duet and its R&B performance award.

sources.title: MusicRadar: Mick Hucknall on George Michael’s Aretha Franklin duet
sources.evidence: The article identifies the duet and its performers, alongside Hucknall’s recollection of hearing about the collaboration.

entries.claim: Christina Aguilera performed Etta James’s signature song “At Last” at James’s funeral.

sources.title: NME: Christina Aguilera performs At Last at Etta James’s funeral
sources.evidence: The report describes Aguilera’s performance at the memorial, with a performance video. Full article opened via Python urllib.

sources.title: ABC News: Christina Aguilera and Stevie Wonder pay tribute to Etta James
sources.evidence: The memorial report independently describes Aguilera singing At Last and her expressed admiration for James.

metadataChecks.evidence: Apple artist profile dates formation to 2010 in Seoul, distinct from the 2013 debut.
